cards.explanation: The answer is False. The psalm opens with "Praise God in His sanctuary." and then it keeps going. "Praise Him in His mighty heavens." (Psalm 150:1) One verse, and the praise has already walked out the front door and gone upstairs, friends.

The answer is why to praise Him. "Praise Him for His mighty acts; praise Him for His excellent greatness." (Psalm 150:2) Each line says "for," and that little word hands everyone the reason. The psalm just told us where, and now it tells us why.

The answer is True. "Praise Him with tambourine and dancing…" (Psalm 150:4) The tambourine is an instrument, but dancing is just a person moving. So the praise isn't only something you play, friends. It's something you can do with your whole body, and I'd say that's good news for anybody who can't carry a tune.

The answer is loud. "Praise Him with clashing cymbals; praise Him with resounding cymbals." (Psalm 150:5) Cymbals that clash and resound are not tiptoeing around. I think nobody in that band was worried about waking the neighbors.

The answer is every creature with breath. "Let everything that has breath praise the LORD!" (Psalm 150:6) The psalm doesn't pick a job title or a section of the choir. If you've got breath in you, you're on the list, and that includes every one of you, friends.

The answer is True. The psalm opens with "Hallelujah!" and the last line ends with "Hallelujah!" (Psalm 150:1, 6) So the whole psalm is one big hallelujah with a band in the middle, bakers. It's like a cookie box with the same ribbon on both ends.
